findings.statement: CA9 is up in tumour at both layers in CPTAC: RNA log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312] and protein log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]. It ranks second in the convergence ranking and is already hit by girentuximab-type antibodies, and the signal is tumour-intrinsic by purity analysis.

NNMT is strongly up in TCGA-KIRC tumour RNA (log2FC [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.685]), also up at protein in CPTAC, and higher expression predicts worse overall survival (log HR per SD [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301]). It is tumour-intrinsic by purity analysis.

CD70 is up in TCGA-KIRC tumours (log2FC [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.09]) and up at protein in CPTAC. In the GTEx vital-organ proteome it is not organ-enriched (max tissue-specificity score [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34]), a favourable safety signal; CD70 antibodies are in clinical development.

ENPP3 is a membrane enzyme up in tumour RNA and protein in CPTAC and in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC [gene=ENPP3; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.557]). It shows no vital-organ enrichment (tissue-specificity score [gene=ENPP3; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.0]), and an ADC (AGS-16C3F) has reached phase two.

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile; RNA and protein are both up in CPTAC and the TCGA-KIRC replication is strong (log2FC [gene=SCARB1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.989]). It is not prognostic and has no ccRCC-selective dependency, so tractability rests on cholesterol-uptake biology.

SLC16A3 (MCT4 lactate exporter) is up in CPTAC RNA and protein and replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC [gene=SLC16A3; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.291]), consistent with a glycolytic, HIF-driven phenotype; no ccRCC-selective dependency was seen.

PSAT1 is the top-ranked biomarker and is down in tumour (TCGA-KIRC log2FC [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-2.974]), consistent with loss of tubule identity. Higher expression is associated with worse survival (log HR per SD [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.43]), so the direction is counter-intuitive and warrants care.

ALDH6A1 is down in tumour (TCGA-KIRC log2FC [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-2.805]), with protein also down in CPTAC, and is a favourable-prognosis marker (log HR per SD [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554]). Its copy number correlates with expression, a real dosage effect of frequent copy loss.

PCK1, a proximal-tubule gluconeogenic enzyme, is strongly down in tumour (TCGA-KIRC log2FC [gene=PCK1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-3.079]) with concordant protein loss in CPTAC. It is a tubule-identity biomarker, not a target.

SLC6A19, a proximal-tubule amino-acid transporter, is lost in tumour (TCGA-KIRC log2FC [gene=SLC6A19; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-3.221]), with protein also down in CPTAC. It reflects loss of normal tubule identity.

caveats: Several findings quote TCGA RNA values because they are the verified records; CPTAC RNA and protein agree in direction per the convergence ranking.
Cell-line (PRISM, DepMap) dependency data show no ccRCC-selective dependency for the top up-regulated genes, and 2D culture misses HIF-biology.
Down-regulated biomarkers (PSAT1, PCK1, SLC6A19, ALDH6A1) mostly reflect loss of tubule identity and tumour-normal compositional differences.
Not all candidates were checked individually for phosphosites, kinase activity or mutation recurrence; the top candidates are rarely mutated drivers.
Bulk proteomics with 110 tumours and 84 matched normals; the CPTAC protein fold-changes are smaller than RNA because of TMT ratio compression.
